employee_master.title: HR 1 — The Employee Master & Organisational Structure
employee_master.desc: The Employee master in ZhiftERP: the organisational masters (Branch, Department tree with approver tables, Designation, Employment Type, Employee Grade) in build order; the Employee record's identity, joining, organisational, contact, personal, and bank field groups with what reads each field; the joiner verification procedure; the status lifecycle with the two-field exit rule and recorded changes; the Reports To structure and the Organizational Chart page; and the monthly and quarterly register hygiene reads.

lessons.title: Chapter 1 — The Employee master: scope and structure
lessons.html:
This module covers the Employee master in ZhiftERP and the organisational masters it depends on. On completing this module you will be able to: create the organisational masters (Company, Branch, Department, Designation, Employment Type, Grade); create a complete Employee record and explain the purpose of each field group; operate the status lifecycle; build the reporting structure and read the organisational chart; and run the register hygiene checks.

The Employee record's position in the system. Employee is a master doctype. The following records link to it:

1. Salary Structure Assignment and Salary Slip (the Payroll track) — pay is computed for Employee records.
2. Leave Allocation, Leave Application, and Attendance (this track, modules 3-4) — leave and attendance are recorded against Employee records.
3. Appraisal, Training Event, and the lifecycle documents (modules 5-7).
4. The User account — the Employee record links to the person's login; this link scopes employee self-service (the Payroll track, module 4).
5. Expense Claim, Employee Advance, and asset custody records.

Because every one of these reads the Employee record, an error in the record repeats in every linked document until corrected. The verification procedure in Chapter 5 exists for this reason.

Custody. HR owns the Employee register: creation, changes, and status. The permission design follows the Sysadmin track's rules: HR roles hold Create and Write on Employee; other functions hold Read where their work requires it; the employee sees their own record through self-service. Changes to bank details and contact details follow the governed master-data rules stated in the Payroll track (written instruction from the employee, filed on the record).

Build order. The organisational masters are created before Employee records, because Employee fields link to them. The order used in this module:

1. Company (exists from implementation).
2. Branch — one record per physical location.
3. Department — the tree, with each department linked to its company.
4. Designation — one record per job title.
5. Employment Type — the employment categories (Full-time, Part-time, Contract, Intern, and others the business defines).
6. Grade — where the business uses grades, the Employee Grade records with their default salary structures.
7. Employee records, in Chapter 3's field order.

Module contents. Chapter 2: the organisational masters. Chapter 3: the Employee record — identity and joining fields. Chapter 4: the organisational fields. Chapter 5: contact, personal, and bank fields, with the verification procedure. Chapter 6: the status lifecycle and exit fields. Chapter 7: the reporting structure and the organisational chart. Chapter 8: worked example. Chapter 9: review and the module rule.

lessons.title: Chapter 2 — The organisational masters
lessons.html:
Create each master below before creating Employee records. Each section states the doctype, the fields to complete, and the records that read it.

1. Branch. Open Branch (awesome bar) > New. Enter the branch name. Create one record per physical location. Read by: the Employee record's Branch field; branch filters on HR reports; the Payroll Entry's branch filter.

2. Department. Open Department > New. Fields:

• Department name.
• Company — required; departments are per company.
• Parent Department — departments form a tree. Set Is Group on parent nodes that contain sub-departments. Example structure: All Departments > Operations > Warehouse; All Departments > Finance.
• Leave Approver and Expense Approver tables — the users authorised to approve leave applications and expense claims for this department's employees. Module 4 reads the leave approvers; complete these tables when the approvers are known.
• Payroll Cost Center — where the site is configured to default the employee's cost center from the department, set it here. The Payroll track's cost-addressing depends on this value or the per-employee field.

Read by: the Employee record's Department field; department filters on every HR report; the approval routing in modules 3-4.

3. Designation. Open Designation > New. Enter the designation name and, where useful, the required skills and description. Create one record per job title in use — Pharmacist, Warehouse Assistant, Branch Manager, Driver, Accounts Assistant. Read by: the Employee record; Job Opening and Job Offer (module 2); Appraisal templates (module 5). Do not encode seniority into free text on the employee; the Designation record is the single definition of each title.

4. Employment Type. Open Employment Type > New. Create the employment categories the business uses: Full-time, Part-time, Contract, Intern, Probation where the business tracks it as a type. Read by: the Employee record; headcount reports by type; policy rules that differ by category (leave entitlement for contract staff, for example — module 4's leave policies can differ by type).

5. Employee Grade. Where the business uses grades: open Employee Grade > New. Enter the grade name and the Default Salary Structure where grades map to pay packages — this default pre-fills at assignment and is verified against the offer letter per the Payroll track's rules. Read by: the Employee record's Grade field; grade-based reports and policies.

Verification. After creating the masters, run these checks:

1. The Department tree renders correctly (open the Department list in tree view; every node under the correct parent; Is Group set on parents only).
2. Every department carries its company.
3. The Designation list contains one record per real job title, no duplicates, no obsolete titles left active.
4. Approver tables completed on departments where the approvers are known; a note recorded for those pending.

lessons.title: Chapter 3 — The Employee record: identity and joining fields
lessons.html:
Open Employee (awesome bar) > New. This chapter walks the identity and joining fields. Complete them in order.

1. Series. The Employee record is named by naming series (HR-EMP- by default). The series is configured once in the Naming Series tool per the Sysadmin track's rules. Do not rename Employee records after creation; the ID appears on every linked document.

2. First Name, Middle Name, Last Name. Enter the legal names as they appear on the employee's identification documents. The full name prints on the salary slip, the statutory schedules, and every HR document; a name entered casually here is a name wrong on a PAYE certificate later.

3. Gender and Date of Birth. Enter from the identification documents. Date of Birth feeds the retirement-date computation where the business configures a retirement age, and the birthday reads on HR reports.

4. Date of Joining. The first day of employment, from the signed offer or contract. This field is read by:

• The payment-days proration on the first Salary Slip (the Payroll track, module 1).
• Leave allocation proration for the joining year (module 4).
• Length-of-service computations on reports and at exit.

Enter the exact contractual date. Do not enter the date the record was created.

5. Status. New records are created as Active. The full lifecycle is Chapter 6.

6. Company. The employing legal entity. On a multi-company site this field determines which company's payroll, leave policies, and reports include the employee. A person employed by two entities is two Employee records (the Payroll track, module 8).

7. The joining detail fields. Complete the employment section: the offer date and confirmation date where tracked; the contract end date for fixed-term contracts — the contract end date is read by the standing report of expiring contracts, and a blank field there means an expiry nobody is warned about; the notice period in days, read at exit; the probation period where tracked.

8. Attachments. Attach at creation: the signed offer or contract, the identification document, and the completed joining forms. The record with its attachments is the employment file's system copy; module 2's onboarding procedure (in the recruitment module) generates part of this automatically when the hire comes through the recruitment pipeline.

Save. Save the record. The organisational fields (Chapter 4) and the contact, personal, and bank sections (Chapter 5) complete the record before the joiner verification (Chapter 5) signs it off.

Note on record creation paths. An Employee record is created either directly (this chapter) or from an accepted Job Applicant through the recruitment pipeline (module 2, Chapter 7). The fields and the verification are identical on both paths; the pipeline pre-fills what the applicant record already holds.

lessons.title: Chapter 4 — The Employee record: organisational fields
lessons.html:
Complete the organisational section of the Employee record. Each field below links to a Chapter 2 master and drives specific behaviour.

1. Branch. Select the employee's branch. Read by branch filters on attendance, leave, and payroll reports.

2. Department. Select from the department tree. Read by: report grouping; the approver routing (the department's Leave Approver and Expense Approver tables apply to this employee unless a per-employee approver overrides them); the cost-center default where configured at department level.

3. Designation. Select the job title. Read by reports, the appraisal machinery (module 5), and the recruitment records when the position is later re-hired.

4. Reports To. Select the employee's direct manager (another Employee record). This field builds the reporting hierarchy:

• The Organizational Chart page (Chapter 7) renders from this field.
• Approval routing can follow it where the site is configured to route to the reporting manager.
• Every employee except the top of the structure has a value here. A blank Reports To on a non-executive record is a data gap; the Chapter 8 verification lists them.

5. Grade. Select where grades are in use. Where the grade carries a Default Salary Structure, the payroll assignment pre-fills from it and is verified against the offer letter.

6. Employment Type. Select the employment category. Read by headcount reports and type-dependent policies.

7. Holiday List. Select the employee's working calendar. This field is read by:

• Payment-days proration (the Payroll track, module 1) — working days count from this list.
• Leave application day counts (module 4) — holidays inside a leave period do not consume leave balance when the list says so.
• Attendance processing (module 3) — holidays are not absence.

Assign the correct list per working pattern: the standard list for head office; the branch list for locations that work Saturdays. The Holiday List records themselves are built in module 3.

8. Payroll Cost Center. Where the site addresses payroll cost per employee, select the branch or unit cost center. The Payroll track, module 1, Chapter 2 states the consequence: a blank value posts salary cost to the company fallback and distorts the branch profit reads. Where the department-level default is configured instead, verify the department carries it.

9. Leave Approver and Expense Approver (per-employee). Where a specific employee's approvals route differently from their department's tables, set the per-employee approver fields. Otherwise leave them blank and let the department tables govern.

Verification. After completing the section, confirm: every organisational field selected from its master (no blanks except documented ones); Reports To present; Holiday List matching the actual working pattern; the cost-center value present at whichever level the site's design placed it.

lessons.title: Chapter 5 — Contact, personal, and bank sections; the joiner verification
lessons.html:
Complete the remaining sections, then run the verification procedure.

1. Contact details.

• Preferred Contact Email — select Company Email or Personal Email, and complete the selected field. This is the address the system uses for salary slip delivery (the Payroll track, module 4) and HR notifications. Verify the address by sending one test message before relying on it.
• Mobile — the employee's number, used for records and for the identity call-back rule (the Payroll track's confidentiality procedures call back the number on record).
• Current Address and Permanent Address — enter from the employee's declaration. The state of residence derived from the current address is read by the PAYE state-split (the Payroll track, module 2, Chapter 5); it is mandatory at joining and updated only on the employee's written notice.
• Emergency contact — name, relation, number. Verify the number is complete; this field is read once, on the day it matters.

2. Personal details. Marital status, blood group where tracked, and the identification numbers the business records (national identification, tax identification for the statutory chain). Enter identification numbers exactly as printed on the documents and attach the document scans.

3. Bank details. Bank Name and Bank A/C No. Rules, restated from the Payroll track:

1. Enter from the employee's own written instruction; attach the instruction to the record.
2. Changes are governed events: verified with the employee through a known channel, never actioned from a forwarded message.
3. The Salary Mode field (Bank, Cash, Cheque) is completed with the bank fields.

4. Health and other sections. Complete per the business's policy on what is recorded. Health details are sensitive personal data; the access rules on the Employee doctype govern who can read them, and the register hygiene read (Chapter 8) confirms the permission matrix covers them.

The joiner verification procedure. Run before the employee's first payroll and before self-service access is issued:

1. Open the Employee record beside the physical or scanned file: the offer letter, the identification documents, the bank instruction, the address declaration.
2. Confirm each field group against its source: names and dates against identification; Date of Joining against the contract; bank fields against the instruction; addresses against the declaration.
3. Confirm the organisational fields (Chapter 4's verification list).
4. Confirm the attachments are on the record.
5. Record the verification in the record's comments: date, verified by. The Payroll track's run checklist (its module 3, line 1) assumes this comment exists.

The verification takes approximately five minutes per joiner. Every downstream document inherits any error this procedure would have caught.

lessons.title: Chapter 6 — The status lifecycle and exit fields
lessons.html:
The Status field controls whether the employee participates in the system's processes. This chapter states each status, what sets it, and what reads it.

The statuses.

1. Active — the working state. The employee appears in payroll runs (Get Employees selects Active employees with assignments), leave allocations, attendance processing, and headcount reports.
2. Inactive — a non-working state without termination, used per the business's policy for long unpaid absence categories where the site distinguishes them. An Inactive employee is excluded from runs. Document the reason in the record when using this status.
3. Suspended — where the business's disciplinary policy uses suspension and the site tracks it as a status. The pay consequence of a suspension is a decision executed through the Payroll track's lanes (leave without pay records, or the documented decision), not an automatic effect of the status alone; confirm the site's configuration and record the decision.
4. Left — the exit state. Set with the Relieving Date.

The exit fields. On confirmation of an exit (the Payroll track, module 7 holds the full exit procedure; this section is the HR side):

1. Relieving Date — the last day of service, from the accepted resignation or the decision letter. Read by: the final slip's proration; the leave balance cutoff and encashment; exclusion from subsequent runs.
2. Status → Left — set effective the relieving date.
3. Reason for Leaving — select or enter per the business's categories (resignation, contract end, termination, retirement). Read by the attrition reports.
4. Leave Encashed — where the exit includes encashment, the flag and its linked Leave Encashment record (the Payroll track, module 7, Chapter 3).
5. Exit interview fields — where the business records exit interviews, complete the fields or attach the interview record. Module 7 of this track covers the exit interview procedure.

The two-field rule. Relieving Date and Status are set the day the exit is confirmed. The Payroll track states the consequence of delay: a leaver who remains Active continues to be selected by payroll runs. The HR action and the payroll checklist line reference the same two fields.

Status changes are recorded events. Every status change carries a comment or an attached document stating the reason and the authority: the resignation letter, the decision letter, the policy reference for an Inactive period. The Version history on the Employee record (track changes is confirmed on for Employee per the Sysadmin track's audit rules) records who changed the status and when; the comment records why.

What is never done. Employee records are not deleted. A record with history is retired by status, never removed; deletion breaks every linked document and removes the employment history the statutory retention rules require the business to keep. The Deleted Document review (the Sysadmin track, module 8) treats a deleted Employee record as a finding.

lessons.title: Chapter 7 — The reporting structure and the organisational chart
lessons.html:
The Reports To field (Chapter 4) builds the reporting structure. This chapter covers reading it, maintaining it, and the approval routing that uses it.

The Organizational Chart page. Open Organizational Chart (awesome bar). The page renders the hierarchy from the Reports To fields: each node an employee, children the employees who report to them. Use the page for:

1. Structure verification — the rendered chart matches the intended structure; a misplaced node is a wrong Reports To value, corrected on the Employee record.
2. Orphan detection — employees missing from the tree below the top node have blank or wrong Reports To values.
3. Span reading — the number of direct reports per manager is visible per node; the business reads it for structure decisions.

Maintaining the structure. Reporting changes are Employee-record edits with the standing disciplines:

1. A manager change is an edit to Reports To on each affected report, made on the documented decision (the transfer memo, the promotion record — module 7 of this track covers the lifecycle documents that carry these changes).
2. A manager's exit re-points their reports before or at the relieving date. Add this line to the exit checklist for any leaver with direct reports: the Organizational Chart page after the exit shows no orphaned nodes.
3. Department moves and Reports To changes are made together when a transfer changes both; the Employee Transfer document (module 7) applies both properties from its date.

Approval routing. Two routing designs exist on the site; know which is configured:

1. Department-table routing — leave applications and expense claims route to the approvers listed on the employee's Department (Chapter 2). This design survives manager changes without per-employee edits.
2. Per-employee routing — the Leave Approver / Expense Approver fields on the Employee record name the approver directly. This design overrides or replaces the department tables per the site's configuration.

The maintenance consequence differs: department-table routing is maintained on a handful of Department records; per-employee routing must be swept when an approver leaves or moves. The register hygiene read (Chapter 8) includes the sweep for sites using per-employee routing: filter the Employee list by each approver field value and confirm every named approver is a current, appropriate holder.

The employee-number reads. Two standing lookups from the Employee list serve the structure:

1. Headcount by dimension — the list grouped by Company, Branch, Department, Designation, Employment Type, or Grade answers headcount questions without a report build. Filter Status = Active for current headcount.
2. The joiners and leavers lists — filtered by Date of Joining or Relieving Date within the period. The Payroll track's headcount reconciliation (its module 3) uses these lists; HR produces them.

lessons.title: Chapter 8 — Worked example: the HealthTrade employee master
lessons.html:
This chapter applies Chapters 2-7 to HealthTrade (the pharmaceutical distributor used across the programme: Head Office plus three branches — Central/Lagos, Ibadan, Akure — approximately thirty staff). Configuration values and findings are listed per step.

Step 1 — organisational masters (Chapter 2).

• Branch: four records — Head Office, Central Lagos, Ibadan, Akure.
• Department tree: All Departments > Operations (Is Group) > Warehouse, Dispatch; All Departments > Retail (Is Group) > Pharmacy Counter; All Departments > Finance; All Departments > Administration. Each department linked to the company. Leave Approver tables completed on Operations, Retail, and Finance with the respective managers.
• Designation: eleven records covering the titles in use (Pharmacist, Pharmacy Technician, Warehouse Assistant, Driver, Branch Manager, Accounts Assistant, and others). Two obsolete titles from the implementation era found in the list and disabled.
• Employment Type: Full-time, Contract, Intern.
• Grade: not used; the field left ungoverned by decision, recorded.

Step 2 — the record sweep (Chapters 3-5). The thirty existing Employee records are verified against files using the Chapter 5 procedure. Findings, each corrected on the record with its source attached:

1. Four records with Personal Email entered but Preferred Contact Email unset — delivery had been failing silently for these four; set and test-messaged.
2. Two records with blank Payroll Cost Center (already found by the Payroll track's walk; corrected there; confirmed here).
3. Three records with Date of Joining equal to the record-creation date rather than the contractual date — corrected from the contracts; one produced a leave-allocation correction in module 4.
4. Six records without identification attachments — collected and attached.
5. One bank account number failing verification against the written instruction — corrected (also found in the Payroll track's walk).

Step 3 — the reporting structure (Chapter 7). Reports To completed on all thirty records. The Organizational Chart page renders: the MD at the top; three branch managers and the finance lead reporting to the MD; branch staff under their managers. Findings: two warehouse staff pointed at a supervisor who left the previous year — re-pointed to the current supervisor; one node orphaned by a blank Reports To — completed.

Step 4 — the routing decision (Chapter 7). Department-table routing is confirmed as the design (fewer records to maintain). The per-employee approver fields are swept and cleared where they duplicated the department tables; one deliberate override retained and documented (a head-office employee whose leave routes to the MD directly).

Step 5 — the standing reads instituted. Monthly: the joiners and leavers lists produced for the payroll reconciliation; the blank-field filters run (Reports To, Holiday List, Preferred Contact Email, Payroll Cost Center — target zero blanks); the contract-expiry report read for the ninety-day window. Quarterly: the approver sweep confirmed against the department tables; the attachment completeness sample (five records checked against files).

Result. Thirty verified records, eleven corrections applied at the sweep, four standing monthly filters at zero blanks, and the organisational chart rendering the actual structure. The register is ready for modules 3-4, which read it every day.

lessons.title: Chapter 9 — Common errors and the module rule
lessons.html:
The errors that recur on the Employee register, each with its correction and prevention.

Error 1 — the incomplete record. Symptom: payroll, leave, or delivery failures traced to blank fields (Holiday List, Preferred Contact Email, Payroll Cost Center, Reports To). Correction: complete the field from its source document. Prevention: the joiner verification procedure (Chapter 5) before first payroll, and the monthly blank-field filters (Chapter 8) at target zero.

Error 2 — the record-creation date entered as Date of Joining. Symptom: first-month proration wrong; leave allocation wrong for the joining year; length-of-service reports wrong. Correction: the contractual date entered from the contract; downstream corrections through the Payroll track's lanes where a slip already computed. Prevention: the verification procedure checks the date against the contract explicitly.

Error 3 — organisational data in free text. Symptom: job titles, branches, or types typed as text variants instead of selected from masters; reports that cannot group. Correction: the master record created or corrected; the employee fields re-selected. Prevention: the build order (masters before employees) and the Sysadmin track's rule that reportable fields are links to masters.

Error 4 — the stale reporting structure. Symptom: the organisational chart showing departed managers; approvals routing to people who left; orphaned nodes. Correction: Reports To re-pointed on the affected records. Prevention: the leaver checklist line for any exit with direct reports, and the chart read after each such exit.

Error 5 — the unrecorded status change. Symptom: statuses changed without documented reason or authority; an Inactive period nobody can explain; a Left status with no relieving date. Correction: the document obtained and attached; the fields completed. Prevention: the rule that every status change carries its comment and document, verified by the Version history.

Error 6 — the deleted record. Symptom: an Employee record removed, breaking linked documents and the retention obligation. Correction: restoration through the platform's recovery paths and the Sysadmin track's incident procedure. Prevention: Delete withheld from HR daily roles in the permission matrix; retirement by status only; the Deleted Document review treating any occurrence as a finding.

Review list. Before the quiz, confirm you can: state what links to the Employee record and the consequence of register errors; create the five organisational masters in build order with their key fields; complete the Employee record's identity, joining, organisational, contact, personal, and bank sections, stating what reads each field; run the joiner verification procedure; operate the status lifecycle with the two-field exit rule and the recorded-change rule; maintain the reporting structure and read the Organizational Chart page; and run the monthly and quarterly hygiene reads.

Module rule 1: the Employee record is the master every HR and payroll document reads — built from the organisational masters, completed from source documents, verified before first use, retired by status, and kept complete by the standing filters. Module 2 covers recruitment: the pipeline from Staffing Plan to Employee Onboarding.

recruitment.title: HR 2 — Recruitment & Onboarding
recruitment.desc: Recruitment in ZhiftERP: the six-stage pipeline from Staffing Plan (details table, plan validation, plan-versus-actual) through Job Opening (status discipline, openings read), Job Applicant (status pipeline, source tracking, funnel and aging reads, data handling), Interview (Interview Round skill sets, same-day Interview Feedback), and Job Offer (complete terms table, letter print, offer register) to Employee creation from the applicant and Employee Onboarding from a template with the pre-joining check.

lessons.title: Chapter 1 — The recruitment pipeline
lessons.html:
This module covers recruitment in ZhiftERP: the document pipeline from planned vacancy to onboarded employee. On completing this module you will be able to: create a Staffing Plan; create and manage Job Openings; process Job Applicants through their status pipeline; schedule and record Interviews with structured feedback; issue Job Offers; create the Employee record from an accepted applicant; and run Employee Onboarding from a template.

The pipeline. Recruitment runs through six doctypes, in order. Learn the sequence; each chapter walks one stage.

1. Staffing Plan — the approved vacancies per designation for a period, with estimated costs (Chapter 2).
2. Job Opening — one advertised position (Chapter 3).
3. Job Applicant — one candidate for an opening, with a status pipeline (Chapter 4).
4. Interview — scheduled assessment events with structured feedback (Chapter 5).
5. Job Offer — the offer document with its terms table and status (Chapter 6).
6. Employee + Employee Onboarding — the record created from the accepted applicant, and the onboarding task list generated from a template (Chapter 7).

Why the pipeline is used rather than informal hiring. Each stage produces a record, and the records produce three things informal hiring cannot:

1. Traceability — every hire traces from its vacancy through its interviews to its offer; every offer's terms are on a document; the Employee record created at the end pre-fills from verified pipeline data instead of retyped notes.
2. Control — hiring against the Staffing Plan means vacancies are approved before they are advertised; offers are issued from a document with an approval, not from a conversation.
3. Reporting — time-to-hire, source effectiveness, and pipeline counts read from the records.

Custody. HR operates the pipeline. The hiring decisions belong to the deciding managers and the owner per the business's approval design: the Staffing Plan's approval authorises the headcount and budget; the offer's terms follow the approved decision. The operator's rule from the Payroll track applies unchanged: no record without its approved decision, and the record states exactly what the decision stated.

Interaction with module 1. The pipeline ends where module 1 begins: the Employee record. The joiner verification (module 1, Chapter 5) runs identically for pipeline hires; the pipeline reduces the retyping, not the verification.

Module contents. Chapter 2: Staffing Plan. Chapter 3: Job Opening. Chapter 4: Job Applicant. Chapter 5: Interview. Chapter 6: Job Offer. Chapter 7: Employee creation and Employee Onboarding. Chapter 8: worked example. Chapter 9: review and the module rule.

lessons.title: Chapter 2 — The Staffing Plan
lessons.html:
Open Staffing Plan (awesome bar) > New. The Staffing Plan records the approved vacancies for a period. Complete the fields in order.

1. Name and Company. Name the plan for its period and scope: 2026 H2 — Operations. Select the company.

2. From Date and To Date. The period the plan covers. Job Openings created against the plan are validated within this period.

3. The Staffing Details table. One row per designation being planned:

• Designation — from the Designation master (module 1, Chapter 2).
• Number of Positions — the approved vacancy count for the period.
• Current Count — the current headcount in that designation; the system computes the current count from Active Employee records where configured, and the row shows current against planned.
• Estimated Cost Per Position — the annual cost estimate used for the plan's budget total.
• Total Estimated Cost — computed per row; the plan totals the rows.

4. Department scoping. Where the plan is scoped to a department, set it; company-wide plans leave the scope broad. Use one plan per approval decision — a plan is an approved document, and its rows are the approved numbers.

5. Submit. The Staffing Plan is a submittable document. Submission records the approval state; amendments follow document rules.

What the plan controls. With staffing plans in use, Job Opening creation validates against the plan: an opening for a designation is checked against the planned positions for the period, and openings beyond the plan are blocked or flagged per the site's configuration. This is the control stated in Chapter 1: vacancies are approved before they are advertised. Where the validation blocks a genuinely needed opening, the correction is a plan amendment through its approval, not a bypass.

The plan's reads.

1. Plan versus actual — the plan's rows against current Active headcount per designation: positions filled, positions open, positions over plan.
2. The budget read — the plan's total estimated cost is the hiring budget's document; the owner approved this number, and the review round's salary modelling (the Payroll track, module 6) reads beside it.
3. The period close — at the plan period's end, the plan is read against outcomes: positions filled within period, positions lapsed, cost against estimate. The next period's plan is drafted from this read.

Practical procedure: draft the plan rows with the deciding managers, attach the approval, submit, and only then open Chapter 3's openings. A hire that starts at the opening instead of the plan has skipped the approval that the pipeline exists to enforce.

lessons.title: Chapter 3 — The Job Opening
lessons.html:
Open Job Opening (awesome bar) > New. One Job Opening is one advertised position. Complete the fields in order.

1. Job Title. The advertised title. Keep it consistent with the Designation; the advertisement can elaborate, the designation stays canonical.

2. Designation. Select from the Designation master. This link connects the opening to the Staffing Plan validation (Chapter 2) and to the applicant and offer records downstream.

3. Company, Department, and Location. Select the employing company; the department and the branch or location fields per the position. These fields pre-fill downstream records and scope the reports.

4. Staffing Plan. Link the opening to its plan row where plans are in use. The validation runs on this link.

5. Status. Open or Closed. An Open opening accepts applicants; close the opening when the position is filled or withdrawn. Closing is a deliberate act: the pipeline reads count open positions from this status, and a filled position left Open overstates the vacancy report.

6. Description. The role description: responsibilities, requirements, and terms summary as the business publishes them. Write the description once here; the applicant-facing publication and the interview rounds (Chapter 5) both read from it.

7. Publication. Where the site publishes openings to the website portal, the publish setting on the opening controls listing. Where the business advertises externally (job boards, referrals), record the channels used — Chapter 4's source tracking reads them.

The opening's lifecycle.

1. Created against the plan; status Open.
2. Applicants attach to it (Chapter 4) as they apply.
3. Interviews and offers proceed for shortlisted applicants (Chapters 5-6).
4. On acceptance and joining, the opening is Closed with a note of the hire; on withdrawal, Closed with the reason.

The openings read. The Job Opening list filtered by Status = Open is the live vacancy report: each row's age (creation date to today) is the time-open figure, and openings aging beyond the business's expected time-to-fill are flagged to the hiring manager. Run this read monthly with the plan-versus-actual read (Chapter 2).

One opening per position. Create one opening per vacancy instance where positions are tracked individually, or one opening with the position count per the business's practice — decide once and record the convention, because the vacancy reports count differently under each convention and a mixed register counts nothing reliably.

lessons.title: Chapter 4 — The Job Applicant
lessons.html:
Open Job Applicant (awesome bar) > New — or receive records created by the portal where applications arrive online. One record per candidate per opening. Complete or verify the fields in order.

1. Applicant Name and Email Address. The candidate's name and contact email. The email is the pipeline's communication channel; verify it is entered correctly on manually created records.

2. Job Opening. Link the applicant to the opening applied for. A candidate applying for two openings is two applicant records; the records track independently.

3. Source. Select the Job Applicant Source — the channel that produced the candidate (Website, Referral, the named job board, Walk-in). Create the source records once in the Job Applicant Source master. The source field feeds the effectiveness read: applicants and hires per source, which tells the business where its advertising money produces hires.

4. The resume and documents. Attach the candidate's resume and any submitted documents to the record. The record is the candidate's file; interviewers read from it (Chapter 5), and the offer stage reads it again.

5. Status. The applicant status pipeline. The standard values and their use:

1. Open — received, not yet processed.
2. Replied — contact made; in process (screening, interviewing).
3. Hold — parked with a reason recorded (a strong candidate for a later vacancy; a process pause).
4. Rejected — not proceeding; set with the courtesy communication sent. Reject formally rather than by silence: unanswered applicants judge the business by the silence, and the status left Open forever makes the pipeline reads meaningless.
5. Accepted — offer accepted; proceeds to Employee creation (Chapter 7).

The pipeline reads.

1. The funnel count — applicants per status per opening: how many received, in process, on hold, rejected, accepted. Read weekly during active hiring; a stage where candidates accumulate without moving is the process bottleneck to fix.
2. The aging read — days since last status change per active applicant. Candidates aging at Open are unprocessed applications; candidates aging at Replied are a slow interview stage.
3. The source read — applicants and eventual hires grouped by Source, quarterly.

Data handling. Applicant records contain personal data of people who may never join the business. Apply the standing confidentiality rules: access limited to the recruiting roles; documents stored on the record, not in personal drives; and a retention convention decided and recorded — how long rejected applicants' records and documents are kept, and the periodic clearing per that convention.

lessons.title: Chapter 5 — The Interview
lessons.html:
Interviews are scheduled and recorded through two doctypes: the Interview Round (the reusable definition of an assessment stage) and the Interview (one scheduled event for one applicant). Build the rounds once; schedule interviews per applicant.

1. The Interview Round. Open Interview Round (awesome bar) > New. One record per assessment stage per role family:

• Round Name — Technical Screen — Pharmacist, Final Interview — Management.
• Designation — the role family the round applies to.
• Interviewers — the default panel: the users who conduct this round.
• Expected Skill Set — the skills table: one row per skill the round assesses. This table defines the feedback form's structure (see the Interview Feedback below); write the skills as assessable items (dispensing accuracy, regulatory knowledge, team supervision), because interviewers will rate exactly these rows.

2. The Interview. Open Interview > New per scheduled event:

• Job Applicant and Interview Round — the candidate and the stage.
• Scheduled On, From Time, To Time — the schedule. The interviewers receive the event per the site's notification configuration.
• Interviewers — pre-filled from the round; adjust per event where the panel differs.
• Status — Pending, Under Review, Cleared, Rejected. Update the status as the event concludes; the applicant's pipeline position (Chapter 4) is read alongside it.

3. The Interview Feedback. Each interviewer submits an Interview Feedback record against the Interview: the skills table from the round rendered as rating rows, plus the overall result and remarks. The design's purpose:

1. Structured comparison — every candidate for the round is rated on the same skill rows; the comparison across candidates is row by row, not impression against impression.
2. Recorded basis — the hire and reject decisions have recorded assessments behind them. Write remarks that state observations, not speculation: what the candidate demonstrated, against the skill row.
3. Independent submission — each interviewer submits their own feedback record; panel discussions follow the submissions where the business's practice wants calibration.

The interview procedure, per applicant.

1. Shortlist decision recorded on the applicant (status Replied, remark stating the shortlist).
2. Interview created against the applicable round; scheduled; the candidate informed.
3. Event conducted; each interviewer submits Interview Feedback the same day (feedback written later is reconstructed impression, not assessment).
4. Interview status updated (Cleared or Rejected); the applicant's status and next stage follow.
5. Multi-round processes repeat steps 2-4 per round; the applicant's record accumulates the full assessment history.

Practical procedure: build the Interview Rounds for the standing role families once, with the hiring managers defining the skill rows. A hiring process with defined rounds runs the same regardless of who schedules it, and its records support every later question about how the decision was made.

lessons.title: Chapter 6 — The Job Offer
lessons.html:
Open Job Offer (awesome bar) > New. The Job Offer is the offer's document of record. Complete the fields in order.

1. Job Applicant. Select the candidate. The applicant's details pre-fill.

2. Company and Designation. The employing entity and the offered position, from the masters.

3. Offer Date. The date the offer is issued.

4. The Job Offer Terms table. One row per term of the offer: the offer term (from the Offer Term master — Base Salary, Probation Period, Notice Period, Annual Leave, and the other terms the business states) and its value. Rules:

1. The terms entered here are the terms the approved hiring decision stated — the Chapter 1 custody rule: the record states exactly what the decision stated.
2. The pay term entered here is the figure the Payroll track's assignment will carry as Base; the offer document and the assignment must agree, and the joiner verification checks them against each other.
3. Terms not in the table are not offered. The table is the complete statement; side communications that vary it create the disputes the document exists to prevent.

5. Status. Awaiting Response → Accepted or Rejected. Update on the candidate's response; the status drives the pipeline reads and Chapter 7's Employee creation.

6. The offer letter print. The Job Offer prints as the offer letter through its print format: the letterhead, the terms table, the validity and conditions text per the business's template. The print rules from the Sysadmin track apply: identity from the letterhead, terms from the document, nothing hard-typed into the format. The signed acceptance (physical or per the business's acceptance process) attaches to the Job Offer record.

The offer procedure.

1. The hiring decision approved per the business's design (the deciding manager and the owner per the approval ladder; the pay figure inside the Staffing Plan's budget or separately approved).
2. The Job Offer created with the complete terms table; reviewed against the decision; submitted.
3. The offer letter printed and issued; the validity period stated.
4. The response recorded: Accepted with the signed acceptance attached, or Rejected with the reason noted (the reasons read quarterly — offers rejected on pay tell the business its figures are off market).
5. On acceptance: the applicant status moves to Accepted, and Chapter 7's creation procedure runs.

The offer register read. The Job Offer list is the standing register: offers outstanding (Awaiting Response, with age), acceptance rate per period, and the rejection reasons. Read monthly during active hiring.

lessons.title: Chapter 7 — Employee creation and Employee Onboarding
lessons.html:
The pipeline's last stage: the accepted applicant becomes an Employee record, and the Employee Onboarding document generates the joining task list.

1. Creating the Employee from the applicant. From the accepted Job Applicant (or the accepted Job Offer per the site's flow), use the create-Employee action. The system creates the Employee record pre-filled with the pipeline's data: name, contact email, designation, company. Then:

1. Complete the record per module 1, Chapters 3-5: the joining fields (Date of Joining from the accepted offer's agreed start date), the organisational fields, the contact, personal, and bank sections.
2. Attach the pipeline documents that belong on the employment file: the signed offer and acceptance (linked via the Job Offer), the identification documents collected at acceptance.
3. Run the joiner verification (module 1, Chapter 5) — identical for pipeline hires; the pipeline pre-fill reduces retyping, not verification.
4. Close the Job Opening (Chapter 3) with the hire noted.

2. The Employee Onboarding Template. Open Employee Onboarding Template (awesome bar) > New — built once per role family or company-wide:

• Company, and the Department/Designation scope where templates differ by role.
• The Activities table — one row per onboarding task: the activity name, the user or role responsible, the required days (the deadline relative to the boarding start), and whether the task is required before the joining date. Standard activity rows: employment file completed and verified (HR); workstation and tools prepared (Administration); system access created per the joiner procedure (the sysadmin — the Sysadmin track's joiner checklist is this row's content); payroll assignment created and previewed (the payroll operator — the Payroll track's joiner lines); orientation session scheduled (HR/manager); statutory registrations confirmed (PFA, tax — the accountant/HR).

3. The Employee Onboarding document. Open Employee Onboarding > New (or create from the accepted applicant per the flow):

• The employee (or applicant), the joining date, the template.
• On submission the system generates the activity tasks from the template — a project/task set assigned to the responsible users with their deadlines.
• Boarding Status tracks completion: Pending → In Process → Completed. The document is the joining checklist with owners and dates, visible as a list instead of held in one person's memory.

4. The completion read. The onboarding is Completed when every activity closes. Two rules:

1. Activities marked required-before-joining are confirmed complete before the joining date — the joiner who arrives to no workstation, no access, and no payroll assignment is the failure this document prevents, and the pre-joining check is a dated line, not a hope.
2. The onboarding document's completion is read at the first payroll close for the joiner: the Payroll track's checklist line 1 (joiner verified and assigned) corresponds to this document's payroll activities.

Practical procedure: build the template with each responsible function contributing its own rows — the sysadmin writes the access row's content, the payroll operator the assignment row's — so the template is the cross-functional joining procedure in one document.

lessons.title: Chapter 8 — Worked example: a HealthTrade hire end to end
lessons.html:
This chapter runs one hire through Chapters 2-7. Configuration values and outcomes are listed per stage.

Stage 1 — the plan (Chapter 2). The 2026 H2 Staffing Plan for Retail is drafted with the branch managers: rows for Pharmacist (positions 2, current count 4, estimated cost per position entered from the accountant's package figures) and Pharmacy Technician (positions 1). The MD approves; the plan submits. Total estimated cost recorded as the half-year hiring budget line.

Stage 2 — the opening (Chapter 3). A Job Opening is created: Job Title Pharmacist (Akure), Designation Pharmacist, Department Retail > Pharmacy Counter, location Akure, linked to the plan row, status Open. The description is written once on the opening. The advertisement runs on one job board and the staff referral channel; both exist as Job Applicant Source records.

Stage 3 — the applicants (Chapter 4). Nine applicant records accumulate over three weeks: six from the job board, three referrals. Weekly funnel read: week two shows five records aging at Open — the screening backlog is cleared the same week and the read returns to normal. Three candidates shortlist (status Replied, shortlist remarks); six are formally rejected with the courtesy message, statuses set.

Stage 4 — the interviews (Chapter 5). The Pharmacist role family's two Interview Rounds exist from the build: Technical Screen (skills: dispensing accuracy, regulatory knowledge, inventory handling; panel: the senior pharmacist and the Akure branch manager) and Final Interview (skills: customer handling, team fit, availability; panel: the MD and the branch manager). Three Technical Screens run in one week; each interviewer submits Interview Feedback the same day. Two candidates clear to Final; one is rejected on the recorded ratings. Finals run; one candidate clears with consistent ratings across both interviewers.

Stage 5 — the offer (Chapter 6). The hiring decision approves per the ladder; the Job Offer is created with the full terms table: Base Salary (the figure the assignment will carry), Probation Period six months, Notice Period one month, Annual Leave per policy. The offer letter prints on the letterhead and issues with a two-week validity. The candidate accepts; the signed acceptance attaches; status Accepted. The second finalist is placed on Hold with a remark (a strong candidate for the plan's second position).

Stage 6 — creation and onboarding (Chapter 7). The Employee record is created from the applicant, pre-filled; the joining sections complete from the collected documents; the joiner verification runs and its comment is recorded. The Employee Onboarding document generates from the company template: eight activities across HR, Administration, the sysadmin, and the payroll operator. The pre-joining check on the joining date's eve: workstation ready, access created, payroll assignment created and previewed against the offer (the Base matching the offer's term row). The pharmacist joins on the agreed date; the opening closes with the hire noted; boarding status reaches Completed in the first week.

Stage 7 — the reads. The quarter's recruitment reads: time-to-hire for the position, 41 days from opening to joining; source read, the hire from the job board, two of three shortlists from referrals; the plan-versus-actual row updated (one of two Pharmacist positions filled). The records answer each read without reconstruction.

lessons.title: Chapter 9 — Common errors and the module rule
lessons.html:
The errors that recur in the recruitment pipeline, each with its correction and prevention.

Error 1 — hiring outside the plan. Symptom: openings and offers for positions no plan approved; headcount and cost growing without an approval trail. Correction: the plan amended through its approval to cover the position, or the opening withdrawn. Prevention: the plan-first order enforced; the opening's plan link and the plan validation in use.

Error 2 — the informal offer. Symptom: terms communicated in conversation or free-form messages; the Job Offer absent or created after acceptance; the assignment's Base disagreeing with what the candidate was told. Correction: the Job Offer created with the complete terms table and reconciled with the candidate before joining. Prevention: the rule that the offer is issued from the document, and the joiner verification's check that the assignment Base equals the offer's pay term.

Error 3 — the silent rejection. Symptom: applicant records aging at Open indefinitely; candidates never answered; pipeline reads meaningless. Correction: statuses set with the courtesy communication sent. Prevention: the weekly funnel and aging reads during active hiring.

Error 4 — the unstructured interview. Symptom: interviews without rounds or feedback records; decisions with no recorded basis; candidates compared by recollection. Correction: feedback recorded for completed interviews where still possible; rounds built for the role family. Prevention: Interview Rounds with skill rows built before hiring starts, and same-day feedback submission as the standing rule.

Error 5 — the unonboarded joiner. Symptom: the new employee arriving to no access, no workstation, no payroll assignment; the first week spent assembling what should have preceded it. Correction: the missing activities completed immediately through their owners. Prevention: the Employee Onboarding document generated at acceptance, and the pre-joining activities confirmed complete on a dated check before the joining date.

Error 6 — applicant data mishandled. Symptom: resumes and personal documents in personal drives and inboxes; no retention convention; rejected candidates' data kept indefinitely. Correction: documents moved onto the records; the retention convention decided and the clearing performed. Prevention: the data-handling rules of Chapter 4 — access limited, documents on records, retention recorded and executed.

Review list. Before the quiz, confirm you can: state the six-stage pipeline and what each stage's record produces; create a Staffing Plan with its details table and state what the plan validates; create and manage Job Openings with the status discipline and the openings read; process Job Applicants through the status pipeline with the source tracking and the three reads; build Interview Rounds with skill rows and run the interview procedure with same-day structured feedback; issue a Job Offer with the complete terms table and the letter print; and create the Employee from the applicant and run Employee Onboarding from a template with the pre-joining check.

Module rule 2: hiring runs through the pipeline — vacancies approved on the plan, candidates processed on recorded statuses, assessments structured and same-day, offers issued from the document with complete terms, and joiners onboarded on a generated checklist confirmed before the joining date. Module 3 covers attendance and shifts.
